A particle of mass 2 kg moves on a smooth horizontal plane under the action of a single force $\vec F=(3\hat i+4\hat j)$ N. Under this force it is displaced from $(0,0)$ to $(1\text{ m},1\text{ m})$. \end{bankq}

\begin{bankq}[id=SA08-P1-PHY-S2-Q07, source={Score Advanced - Test 08 (22 Apr 2023)}, paper=1, qno=7, type=multi, subtopic={Work}, answer={A}, answer_src=key, difficulty=8, diff_parts={K3 S1 I2 C2 F1}, diff_note={concepts: tractive force for a car with quadratic drag, work, work energy theorem in differential form | steps: work energy theorem in differential form; solve the linear equation for v\^{}2}]
A car of mass m is moving on a horizontal surface with speed v$_0$ along positive x-axis. The driver of car wishes to accelerate the car. He accelerates the car which provides a constant tractive force F, directed along the line of motion of car. The frontal force of resistance is directed opposite to the velocity and given as F$_\text{r}$ = $\alpha$v$^2$ in magnitudes where $\alpha$ is a positive constant and v is speed of car at that time. Assume initially car is at origin. Express the tractive force F as a function of x and v, where x is the displacement of the car and v is the velocity at that position.
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{$\alpha\,\dfrac{\text{v}^2-\text{v}_0^2\text{e}^{\frac{-2\alpha\text{x}}{\text{m}}}}{1-\text{e}^{\frac{-2\alpha\text{x}}{\text{m}}}}$}
\opt{B}{$\alpha\,\dfrac{\text{v}^2+\text{v}_0^2\text{e}^{\frac{-2\alpha\text{x}}{\text{m}}}}{1-\text{e}^{\frac{-2\alpha\text{x}}{\text{m}}}}$}
\opt{C}{$\alpha\,\dfrac{\text{v}^2-\text{v}_0^2\text{e}^{\frac{-2\alpha\text{x}}{\text{m}}}}{1+\text{e}^{\frac{-2\alpha\text{x}}{\text{m}}}}$}
\opt{D}{$\alpha\,\dfrac{\text{v}^2+\text{v}_0^2\text{e}^{\frac{-2\alpha\text{x}}{\text{m}}}}{1+\text{e}^{\frac{-2\alpha\text{x}}{\text{m}}}}$}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=SA14-P1-PHY-S1-Q02, source={Score Advanced - Test 14 (16 May 2023)}, paper=1, qno=2, type=multi, subtopic={Potential energy curves}, answer={A,C,D}, answer_src=key, difficulty=9, diff_parts={K3 S2 I2 C2 F1}, diff_note={concepts: particle in a circular orbit under a given potential, potential energy curves, force from U(r) | steps: force from U(r); circular orbit condition; stability}, also_in={Score Advanced - Test 20 (06 Apr 2024) P1 Q2}]
A non-relativistic particle of mass m is held in a circular orbit around the origin by an attractive force. The potential energy of the force is given by U (r) = $\dfrac{kr^2}{2}$, where r is the distance of the particle from origin and k is a constant. Assuming the Bohr quantization of the angular momentum of the particle, choose the \textbf{correct} (v $\rightarrow$ velocity of particle, KE(r) $\rightarrow$ kinetic energy of particle, E(r) $\rightarrow$ total energy of the particle)
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{r$^2$ = $\dfrac{\text{nh}}{2\pi\sqrt{\text{km}}}$}
\opt{B}{v$^2$ = $\dfrac{\text{nh}}{2\pi\sqrt{\text{km}}}$}
\opt{C}{KE(r) = U(r)}
\opt{D}{E (r) = $\dfrac{\text{nh}}{2\pi}\sqrt{\dfrac{\text{k}}{\text{m}}}$}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}

\begin{bankq}[id=SA15-P1-PHY-S2-Q08, source={Score Advanced - Test 15 (18 May 2023)}, paper=1, qno=8, type=multi, subtopic={Potential energy curves}, answer={A,C}, answer_src=key, difficulty=8, diff_parts={K3 S1 I2 C2 F1}, diff_note={concepts: charged rod swinging in a horizontal electric field, potential energy curves, energy of rod in gravity plus field | steps: energy of rod in gravity plus field; equilibrium angle}]
A uniformly charged non conducting rod is suspended vertically at its end. The rod can swing freely in the vertical plane without any friction. The linear charge density on the rod is $\lambda$ C/m and it has a uniformly distributed mass of $M$. Length of the rod is $L$. A uniform horizontal electric field ($E$) is switched on in the region. Select the correct option/options :-\par
\bfig{52.7}{SA15_p1_phy_s2_q08_1.png}
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{If $E=\dfrac{mg}{\lambda L}$, then rod just manages to make it horizontal}
\opt{B}{If $E=\dfrac{mg}{2\lambda L}$, then rod just manages to make it horizontal}
\opt{C}{If $E=\dfrac{Mg}{\lambda L}$, the rod has maximum kinetic energy at an angle $45^\circ$ with vertical}
\opt{D}{If $E=\dfrac{Mg}{2\lambda L}$, the rod has maximum kinetic energy at an angle $45^\circ$ with vertical}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}

\begin{bankq}[id=SA24-P1-PHY-S1-Q06, source={Score Advanced - Test 24 (17 Apr 2024)}, paper=1, qno=6, type=multi, subtopic={Conservative forces}, answer={A,B}, answer_src=key, difficulty=8, diff_parts={K3 S1 I2 C2 F1}, diff_note={concepts: particle subject to two given forces, conservative forces, work done by each force | steps: work done by each force; conservative or not}]
A particle of mass m is subjected to two forces
\[\vec F_1=f(r)\dfrac{\vec r}{|\vec r|}\quad\text{and}\quad \vec F_2=-\alpha\vec v\]
where f(r) is a real valued function depending on the distance of the particle from the origin, $\vec r$ is the position vector of the particle and $\alpha$ is a positive constant. If at t = 0, $\vec v$ vector is in the x-y plane and the angular momentum of the particle about the origin is $L_0$. Choose the correct option(s).
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{Plane of motion of the particle does not change.}
\opt{B}{Angular momentum of the particle about the origin is given by $L_0e^{-\frac{\alpha t}{m}}$.}
\opt{C}{Angular momentum of the particle about the origin remains constant.}
\opt{D}{The value of angular momentum about the origin will depend on f(r).}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=SA24-P2-PHY-S2-Q08, source={Score Advanced - Test 24 (17 Apr 2024)}, paper=2, qno=8, type=multi, subtopic={Work}, answer={A,C}, answer_src=key, difficulty=8, diff_parts={K3 S1 I2 C2 F1}, diff_note={concepts: particle under a time varying force, work, velocity by integration | steps: velocity by integration; stopping time}]
A particle of mass m start moving at t = 0 due to a force F = $F_0\cos\omega t$, where $F_0$ and $\omega$ are constant. Particle will stop first time at t = $t_0$ and distance travel in this time interval is S, then
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{$T_0=\dfrac\pi\omega$}
\opt{B}{$t_0=\dfrac{\pi}{2\omega}$}
\opt{C}{$S=\dfrac{2F_0}{m\omega^2}$}
\opt{D}{$S=\dfrac{F_0}{m\omega^2}$}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}

When they reach the bottom, then I$_1$ and I$_2$ are the impulses of the weight of the first and the second object during the motion, P$_1$ and P$_2$ are the powers developed by the weight of the first and second objects.\par

\opt{B}{$\dfrac{\mathrm I_1}{\mathrm I_2}=1$}
\opt{C}{$\dfrac{\mathrm I_1}{\mathrm I_2}=\dfrac{\sin\alpha_1}{\sin\alpha_2}$}
\opt{D}{$\dfrac{\mathrm P_1}{\mathrm P_2}=\dfrac{\sin\alpha_1}{\sin\alpha_2}$}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}

\opt{D}{When total work done by a conservative force on the system is positive then the potential energy associated with this force decreases.}
\end{qoptions}
